top5.title: AI Stocks Fall After the U.S. Elections
top5.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, while several chipmakers dropped more than 9% or by double digits. Wall Street fears a slowdown in data centers after the adoption of numerous local measures aimed at restricting them.
top5.why: The post-election 5.5% Nasdaq drop and sharp declines in AI infrastructure stocks show that resistance to data-center expansion is already affecting technology valuations and could constrain future computing capacity.

top5.title: Anthropic Gives METR Internal Access to Measure AI Progress
top5.description: Anthropic gave METR internal access, and the organization estimates that AI capabilities on well-specified tasks are advancing about twice as fast as they were a year ago.
top5.why: METR’s finding that AI capabilities on well-specified tasks are advancing roughly twice as fast as a year ago could materially change companies’ automation plans, risk assessments and investment timelines.

top5.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a model specialized in hacking
top5.description: GPT-6 Cyber is a version of GPT-6 Astra designed to identify security vulnerabilities and write exploits. It scored 48.5% on ExploitGym, compared with 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, but access remains limited through Daybreak Red.
top5.why: OpenAI’s specialized GPT-6 Cyber substantially improves automated vulnerability discovery and exploit development, raising the urgency of defensive security and responsible access controls.

top5.title: Baidu opens the files for its ERNIE 5.5 Flash base model
top5.description: Baidu is providing researchers with the open files for a 280-billion-parameter model, with 14 billion activated per token. ERNIE 5.5 Flash base has a one-million-token context window and can be fine-tuned.
top5.why: Baidu’s release of a 280-billion-parameter, million-token-context model gives researchers and developers a powerful adaptable Chinese foundation model and intensifies global competition over open AI systems.

top5.title: Beijing Blocks SoftBank’s Acquisition of ABB’s Robotics Division
top5.description: China vetoed SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division through its foreign investment oversight body. The decision highlights the growing strategic importance of industrial robots.
top5.why: China’s block on SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division underscores the strategic and geopolitical importance of industrial automation and the growing barriers to cross-border technology deals.
